summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with worsening dizziness and chronic abdominal pain, following a recent hospitalization for culture-negative peritonitis and orthostatic hypotension. She reported persistent dizziness even at rest, which worsened with standing, and generalized abdominal pain exacerbated by peritoneal dialysis. Initial peritoneal fluid showed elevated white blood cells, but repeat testing and cultures were negative for infection, and CT imaging revealed no abscess or acute abdominal process. Orthostatic blood pressure improved after increasing midodrine to 10 mg TID and fludrocortisone to 0.1 mg BID, and discontinuing tizanidine. Symptoms of dysuria resolved after fluconazole and restarting torsemide, with urine culture showing no significant growth. She was discharged on optimized medical therapy with follow-up arranged, and will continue peritoneal dialysis at home.
problems: Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
